text: `adrcheck check --write-baseline` must record the run's stale list to `.adrcheck/baseline.json`, including every stale row.
quote: `adrcheck check --write-baseline` records the run's stale list to `.adrcheck/baseline.json`, every row,

text: Each baseline row must be keyed by ADR number and obligation id and must carry the missing anchors beside it for the reviewer.
quote: keyed by ADR number and obligation id with the missing anchors beside them for the reviewer

text: Later runs must read the baseline file when it exists, keep the rows it names in the report flagged as known, and list only the other stale rows.
quote: Later runs read the file when it exists, keep the rows it names in the report flagged as known, list only the others,

text: Runs that use the baseline must print a count of the known stale rows.
quote: and print a count of the known.

text: Nothing other than a deliberate `--write-baseline` invocation may update the baseline file; ordinary check runs must not write or modify it.
quote: Nothing updates the file except a deliberate `--write-baseline`;

text: The baseline must not hold CONFLICT findings; it holds stale rows only.
quote: The baseline holds stale rows only. CONFLICT findings are per diff,

text: The baseline file format must carry a version so a later key can be added without breaking an old file.
quote: The format is versioned so a later key can be added without breaking an old file.

text: The baseline file must be committed and reviewed like source.
quote: it is committed and reviewed like source.

text: A baseline row must leave the baseline only when the team removes it or rewrites the ADR; rows must not be silently dropped or matched across an ADR edit, since edited ADRs compile to new obligation ids and surface again.
quote: A row leaves the baseline when the team removes it or rewrites the ADR, since an edited ADR compiles to new obligation ids and its rows surface again for review.
